# GitHub Actions Runner

> Projects supply their execution environments. This setup starts them on demand,
> connects them to GitHub Actions, limits capacity, and cleans disposable data.
> Installed software survives jobs and weekly cleanup.

## Use a project-owned image

Keep the Dockerfile and image build in the consuming project's repository.
Publish a versioned image tag to a registry the runner host can pull from.
A Dockerfile in this infrastructure repository is optional.

For Linux, extend the shared image or provide a compatible GitHub Actions runner
image. The deployed shared images on Bob are
`localhost:15000/github-actions-runner-poc:local` (x64) and `:arm64` (ARM64).
That loopback registry is reachable on Bob; builds using it run on Bob.
A project-owned registry is also supported; arrange pull access without baking
credentials or runner registration into the image.

Install required software when building the image. Preserve the runner startup
contract, architecture, runner-owned work directory and configured mount paths.
The current Linux image runs as uid 1001. Prepare writable mount parents before
switching to the runner user. Extending the shared image is the simplest way to
retain its setup; see [the Dockerfile](images/linux/Dockerfile).

For macOS, supply a project-specific prepared Tart base VM instead of a Docker
image. Keep its runner unregistered, with required software installed. Clone a
shared base before changing it. Native release/private runners retain their
existing execution and credential boundaries.

## Connect it to this project's jobs

Match the project's repository URL, scale-set name and architecture in the
installed manager configuration. Change only its `[[scaleset]]` `runner-image`
to the published image tag or Tart base name, before `[scaleset.docker]`:

```toml
[[scaleset]]
# Preserve this entry's existing URL, name, labels and capacity.
runner-image = "REGISTRY/PROJECT-runner:VERSION"
```

This is a fragment for an existing entry, not a complete new scale set.
Workflows select that entry's existing name with `runs-on`. Preserve other scale
sets, shared image tags, services, routing, capacity and security boundaries.
If the project needs different mounts, scope them to its scale set.

Configuration changes require a manager restart after existing jobs finish.
Use the installed service and its graceful drain; never kill active jobs.
Retain the previous image selection for rollback. Run an existing project job
and confirm that it starts and reuses its installed tools. Application test
failures belong to the project; they do not authorize unrelated application fixes.

## Storage contract for weekly cleanup

Ordinary containers and VM clones are disposable. Keep required software in the
image/base VM, or a permanent tool store. Put accumulating data in declared
cleanup locations below the host's CI root.

| Data | Location and cleanup behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Installed software | Image/base VM or `CI_ROOT/tools/PROJECT/`; preserved |
| GitHub setup-action tool installations | `_work/_tool`; preserved |
| Dependency downloads and build caches | `CI_ROOT/caches/PROJECT/`; declare in host `cache_paths` |
| Persistent job output and temporary files | Declare exact disposable paths in `cache_paths` |
| Expiring logs | Declare `log_paths` and retention in the host manifest |
| Reports/journals that must survive | Separate from caches; declare `protected_paths` |

Existing Linux mounts include `/cache/go-mod`, `/cache/go-build`, `/cache/pnpm`,
`/home/runner/_work/_tool`, and tool stores for Vite+, mise and browsers. Inspect
the project's effective mounts: a volume hides software at the same image path.
Seed a new permanent store once, or change only the project's mount so it uses
its image's installation. Never wipe a shared store to activate an image update.
Keep installed software out of cache wipe budgets even when a mount is called
`docker.cache`. Dependency caches may refill after cleanup; toolchains must remain.

For every new persistent mount, record its host path and retention in the host
manifest. Use project-specific stores when versions or settings could affect
other projects. Cleanup clears the contents of declared cache directories, so
never declare a tool directory, retained-evidence directory, or their parent as
a cache. The operator rejects overlaps with protected installations.

For old project image tags, add an explicit project-only `image_retention`
repository prefix and retention days in the host manifest. Configured worker
image tags are protected automatically; use `protected_images` for additional
rollback tags. Host image cleanup does not garbage-collect registry blobs:
configure retention in the project's registry separately. Bob's loopback registry
has no automatic blob cleanup in this operator. Never globally prune Docker,
volumes, registries or Tart VMs. Keep prepared Mac bases and remove only owned,
disposable job data through the existing maintenance policy.

## Installed fleet and operation

- Infrastructure checkout: `/Users/tyler/src/github-actions-runner`.
- Linux host: `ssh bob`; CI root `/srv/github-actions-runner-poc`;
  manager configuration `config/runner.toml` relative to that root.
- Mac CI root: `/Users/tyler/CI/github-actions-runner`;
  manager configuration `poc/config/runner.private.toml` relative to that root.
- Each host's `config/host.json` declares its services, storage and cleanup.
  Inspect it for current paths; [examples](examples/host.json) are templates.
- The signed **GitHub Actions Runner.app** owns macOS background identity.
  Preserve the existing service registrations.

From this Mac, inspect the whole fleet with:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 /Users/tyler/CI/github-actions-runner/bin/fleet.py /Users/tyler/CI/github-actions-runner/config/fleet.json status
```

The scheduled weekly task runs the same operator with `maintain` instead of
`status`. It drains jobs, cleans declared disposable data, and restores services
and routing. Use that existing task; image updates do not need another scheduler
or a fleet-wide cleanup. Keep private host configuration and credentials out of
source control and job images.
